about: Thresholds for the email deliverability trend. scripts/deliverability_trend.py reads this file and takes its CLI defaults from it, so change a rule here and nowhere else. Rates are percentages. The guard-rails are widely quoted rules of thumb, not Bloomreach or mailbox-provider limits for any one project. Each key is explained under notes.

notes.window_days: Default length of the trend window in days (read by the call plan in SKILL.md: the daily query uses 'grouping top' one or two above this). Weeks run Monday to Sunday in the project's time zone, so the first and last week are usually partial; they are marked partial and their rates are still judged.
notes.recent_weeks: The last this-many weeks are 'recent'; the weeks before them are the baseline. Drift compares the pooled recent rate with the pooled baseline rate.
notes.min_baseline_weeks: With fewer judged baseline weeks than this, drift and spikes aren't judged (there's no stable baseline); guard-rails still are.
notes.min_weekly_sends: A week with fewer sends than this is 'low volume': shown, but not judged for spikes or guard-rails, because a handful of bounces swings its rates.
notes.min_breakdown_sends: A sending domain, campaign type, audience group or campaign with fewer sends than this is shown but not judged against the guard-rails.
notes.guardrails: Rule-of-thumb limits. warn crossed is medium priority, limit crossed is high (in a recent week or the recent pool). delivery_rate is delivered / sends and is judged when it falls below. hard and soft bounce rates are of sends; complaint and unsubscribe rates are of delivered. The complaint limits follow the 0.1% / 0.3% spam-rate guidance Gmail and Yahoo published for bulk senders in 2024; the bounce, delivery and unsubscribe limits are common ESP rules of thumb (bounces under about 2%, unsubscribes under about 0.5%). Tune them to the project's own agreements.
notes.drift_ratio: A metric drifts when its pooled recent rate is at least this many times its pooled baseline rate and also at least drift_min_points higher. Delivery rate drifts when it falls by at least drift_min_points.
notes.drift_min_points: Minimum change, in percentage points, for drift to count, per metric, so a move from 0.01% to 0.02% isn't called drift.
notes.spike_ratio: A judged week whose rate is at least this many times the median rate of all judged weeks (the median resists the spike itself), with at least spike_min_events problem events, is a spike. A spike in a recent week is medium priority; an earlier one is low.
notes.spike_min_events: A week needs at least this many of the metric's events (bounces, complaints or unsubscribes) to count as a spike.
notes.top_contributors: How many campaigns to list per spike week and per metric in the campaign breakdown, most problem events first.
notes.status_aliases: Maps the campaign event's status values to the metrics. Projects differ: one tested project records hard_bounced, soft_bounced, complained and unsubscribed; older documentation uses hard_bounce and unsubscribe. Statuses not listed are ignored. Sends are enqueued when the data has any, otherwise sent, otherwise delivered + bounces + failed.
